title: Coast: sky replacement, artificial sunlight, tonal color, and warping

date.basis: Embedded MP4 creation_time, consistent with the Part 3 (2022) folder; may reflect export rather than recording date.

locations.name: Oregon Coast (probable)
locations.basis: Identified by the collection owner, but not independently confirmed by the transcript. Smith Rock State Park is mentioned only as a comparison.

summary: An end-to-end Photoshop workflow that turns a 28 mm coastal frame into a more dramatic, wide-angle-feeling composition. The instructor replaces and rearranges the sky from alternate captures, processes the image in separate tonal zones, fabricates a believable setting sun and its reflected glow, repairs color by tonal range, reshapes the composition with Perspective Warp and Puppet Warp, and finishes with a restrained Auto HDR texture pass.

sections.title: Source frame and baseline dynamic range
sections.description: Reviews the coastal source frame, then establishes a neutral RAW conversion by opening shadows while controlling highlights and exposure.

sections.title: Sky replacement and clone-paint blending
sections.description: Chooses a stronger sky from another capture, explains three replacement scopes, levels the horizon without cropping, and clone-paints clouds and water while protecting the horizon transition.

sections.title: Independent processing of tonal zones
sections.description: Separates sky, flat water, breaking water, and rocks so exposure, warmth, color, and luminosity can be adjusted independently.

sections.title: Creating a sun that was not present
sections.description: Builds a fabricated setting sun in stages using extreme localized RAW adjustments, Gaussian blur, luminosity, Highlight Dodge, History Brush blending, atmospheric warmth, and a matching reflection in the water.

sections.title: Tonal-based color repair
sections.description: Repairs inconsistent water and sun colors by rebuilding color separately across tonal ranges, then uses LAB or Selective Color to control blown yellow.

sections.title: Simulating a wider lens with Perspective Warp
sections.description: Divides the image into sky, land, and water bands, then stretches the periphery into trapezoids to make the 28 mm frame read more like a 14 mm composition.

sections.title: Selective Puppet Warp and blending
sections.description: Demonstrates Puppet Warp control points and locked boundaries, including reshaping a cloud and painting only the warped element back into the unwarped image.

sections.title: Restrained Auto HDR texture
sections.description: Creates an intentionally overprocessed RAW version, then borrows only small amounts at very low opacity to add wave texture or shadow detail while warning against excessive HDR.
